full_judgment: 4. Badsha Mia while owning and possessing 0.19½ acres of land along with others permitted defendant No. 2 to reside there temporarily as he became 'Peer' of Badsha and Badsha was his Murid as religious guide. Tara Banu opposite party No. 2 got her 0.04 acres of land as heirs. Subsequently Chan Mia and Jarina Begum and other heirs of Badsha Mia sold 0.12 acres of land to Tara Banu and in her way Tara Banu became the owner and possessor of 0.16 acres of land and when Nawab Mia husband of Tara Banu went to the Tahshil office for separation of Jama after paying rent on 10-1-91 then came to know that the defendant No. 2 vide Mutations Case No. 354/85-86 mutated his name in respect of 0.54 acres of land in Plot Nos. 166, 167 and 168. Thereafter the plaintiff on 21-1-1991 went to the office of Assistant Commissioner, Akhaura and came to know that a review case was pending against the said mutation case, then the plaintiff filed an application thereon for addition of party and Assistant Commissioner directed the parties to appear before him with necessary papers but the defendant No. 2 failed to show any papers in support of their title, that on 13-2-1991 the defendant No. 2 expressed that his brother-in-law, the defendant No. 1, was the owner of the land on the basis of the title suit and prayed for affirming the order of mutation, on 16-2-1991. The husband of plaintiff No. 1 searched for the suit and on 12-3-1991 after getting certified copy of the same came to know about the collusive compromise judgment and decree of the Title Suit No. 78 of 1988. The plaintiffs of the suit are the owners and possessors of the suit land knowing fully well that the plaintiffs of the instant suit land filed the Title Suit No. 78 of 1988 without making the plaintiffs as parties of the said suit and, as such, prayed for a decree that the compromise decree dated 8-11-1990 passed in Title Suit No. 78 of 1988 was collusive and not binding upon him.
